questions.question: What's the best starting point for choosing an agent framework?
options: The one with the most GitHub stars
A written list of your concrete needs, scored against options that include 'no framework'
questions.explanation: Needs make the decision explicit and revisitable; 'no framework' is the baseline every option must beat.

questions.question: Why are the capability scores in main.py called opinions?
options: They are coarse judgments from Lessons 2–8, written down so a team can argue with specific numbers
They come from an official benchmark
questions.explanation: Writing opinions down turns a vague debate into a specific disagreement you can resolve.

questions.question: When does the tool recommend skipping the framework?
options: When the best framework beats the hand-rolled baseline by less than the margin
When there are more than two needs
questions.explanation: A framework must clearly earn its dependency and learning cost.

questions.question: The audit found api.py importing LangGraph's END and building its config dict. Why is that a problem?
options: The framework has leaked outside the agent module, so switching frameworks means editing more files
questions.explanation: Keep framework code in one boundary module so the choice stays cheap to reverse.

questions.question: You need one agent that returns validated JSON, and dependencies are tightly controlled. What's reasonable?
options: Adopt three frameworks to compare in production
A hand-rolled validate-and-retry loop (like Lesson 8's) may be enough; adopt Pydantic AI if you need more of its features
Use the Claude Agent SDK because it has file tools
questions.explanation: A small, well-understood loop can meet a narrow need without new dependencies.

questions.question: Where should framework imports live in a well-structured agent app?
options: Only in the agent wiring module; tools and API stay framework-free
questions.explanation: Plain-function tools port to any framework, and the API talks to your interface, not framework types.
